findings.title: Unguarded access to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] can raise KeyError
findings.body: The new sender check does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. However `build_integration` only stores `sender` in metadata when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (`if state.get("sender"): integration["metadata"]["sender"] = state["sender"]`), so `sender` is not guaranteed to be present. Existing/older GitHub integrations (created before `sender` was persisted, or created via the pipeline path where no sender state was bound) will have metadata without a `sender` key. In the branch where an `Integration` exists with `status=ACTIVE` but has no `OrganizationIntegration` for the org, this line raises `KeyError` (or `TypeError` if `sender` is not a dict), producing a 500 error page instead of the intended graceful failure. This should use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and fall through to the error page when the sender is unknown.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
findings.body: The test still stubs `GET /app/installations/{id}` as 404, but after this PR the two requests it issues no longer reach `build_integration`: the first `setup_path?...installation_id=...` request has no `state`, so `OAuthLoginView` redirects to GitHub authorize (response discarded), and the second request uses `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which does not match `pipeline.signature`. The resulting `Invalid installation request.` comes from the OAuth state-mismatch branch, not from the 404 handling in `build_integration` (which used to yield `The GitHub installation could not be found.`). As a result the 404/IntegrationError path is now uncovered and the test name is misleading; it should be rewritten to complete the OAuth step with a valid signature and a fresh installation id so it actually reaches `get_installation_info`.

findings.title: OAuth token-exchange network failures are not handled
findings.body: The only error handling in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` wraps `safe_urlread(req)` (catching exceptions during body read). The `safe_urlopen(...)` call that actually performs the token exchange (and the subsequent `get_user_info(...)` call) are outside any try/except, so a GitHub outage, timeout, or 5xx during token exchange raises an unhandled exception and returns a 500 instead of the intended `github-integration-failed.html` page. Since this PR explicitly aims to surface failures in the installation pipeline, these calls should be wrapped and routed to `error(...)` on failure.
